reason: The text demonstrates multiple instances of non-leaders exercising agency. Young men (נְעָרִ֤ים קְטַנִּים) of Bethel actively mock Elisha (2:23), making a choice and taking action independent of leadership. The men of Jericho (אַנְשֵׁ֤י הָעִיר) speak to Elisha and report their problem (2:19), exercising agency in identifying and communicating their needs. The messengers (מַלְאָכִים) sent by King Ahaziah, though subordinates, exercise agency in their missions. Elisha himself, as a disciple rather than established leader, actively refuses to be left behind by Elijah despite repeated commands (2:2, 2:4, 2:6), exercising independent will. While prominent leaders like Ahaziah and Elijah drive major narrative events, the text clearly portrays non-leaders as agents making choices, taking actions, and affecting outcomes.
